quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes to prevent a collision. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: What should you do before turning on the engine?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before turning on the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same. Make this a habit every time you enter your car.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes in advance. This helps drivers behind you know what you are doing and stay at a safe distance.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers may not see you if you are directly behind them. Increase your following distance with these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot. Only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a right turn at this location.

questions.question: What should you never do when changing lanes?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane you want to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Always use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Never change lanes abruptly.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at you.
Only if the pedestrians are not using their phones.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Always stop your vehicle to let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. You may proceed only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: Who must a left-turning driver yield to?

options.text: Cars passing you.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must wait for oncoming traffic to pass. Turn only when it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed to get through it quickly.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid wet areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. These surfaces are slippery and can cause skidding. The safest driving surface is dry and solid.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane with the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. When they are together, only the side with the broken line can pass.

questions.question: A car is following you too closely on a multilane highway. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to match the other car's speed.
Move to the right lane and let the car pass.
Slow down to annoy the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane and let the car pass.
questions.explanation: On highways with multiple lanes, move to the right lane to let the faster car pass. The left lane is for passing slower vehicles.

questions.question: You need to park in an unusual spot. What should you do?

options.text: Park with your backup lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: Always park where your car is visible to drivers coming from any direction. This prevents your parked car from becoming a hazard.

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?

options.text: Information about services for drivers.
Information about road construction and repairs.
Distance information to nearby locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Information about services for drivers.
questions.explanation: Blue signs tell drivers about nearby services like rest areas, food, gas, or hospitals.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Use your signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay in the right lane, as close to the right edge of the road as possible before turning.

questions.question: How should you enter an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop, look for cars, then enter when it is safe.
Look for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and smoothly merge with the traffic already on the highway. Do not stop or slow down.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for them to cross.
Drive around them on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians in a crosswalk cross first. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before moving.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you speed up before turning.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can only turn left onto a one-way street if traffic flows to the left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead.
Merge into another lane.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is coming up.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Drive slower.
Always look carefully around you.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look carefully around you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can be hidden in blind spots. Always watch carefully for them on the road.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you are greeting another driver.
When it can help prevent a crash.
When you are angry with another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it can help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Other drivers may not see you unless they are looking your way. In a dangerous situation, your horn can get their attention. Use your horn when it can help prevent a crash.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. They often make sudden changes in direction. Remember that children and bicycles are small and may be hard to see.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When backing up:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Do not depend only on your rearview or side mirrors because they do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights of oncoming cars at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the speed limit based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit. Slow down for curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare straight ahead at the road.
Focus only on the middle of the road.
Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car. Good drivers stay aware of everything around their vehicle.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
To the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: For a left turn from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to pass before the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, drive through as quickly as possible.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move to the edge nearest you.

questions.question: A tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if you need to. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass until after you see the sign.
Do not pass unless it seems safe.
Do not pass for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass for any reason.
questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign means you must follow the rule. This sign tells you not to pass other vehicles at any time.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or other property, you must attach a note to it. The note must include your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: Bad weather makes it hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you may not see coming.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus turns.
Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: If you try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb, you may crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning before you turn.

questions.question: Why do large trucks need extra space in front of them?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Only to the right.
Only to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look both left and right for cars and pedestrians. Look left a second time because cars from your left will be closer. Look across the intersection to make sure it is clear all the way through before you go.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: One rear wheel should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave the car in "park" when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels so the car will roll away from the road if the brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn your wheels toward it (if going downhill) or away from it (if going uphill).

questions.question: Your car has a two-part safety belt. What should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, buckle your lap belt too.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road gets narrower ahead.
There are many curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are many curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns drivers about a road with many curves.
